physicalNotes: Limbach et al. (2025), Thermal Emission and Confirmation of the Frigid White Dwarf Exoplanet WD 1856+534 b, ApJL (arXiv:2504.16982), Table 1: radius 0.0121 +/- 0.0002 solar radii, mass 0.605 +/- 0.013 solar masses, effective temperature 4920 +/- 50 K. Vanderburg et al. (2020), Nature 585, 363 (arXiv:2009.07282), Table 1, gave 0.0131 +/- 0.00054 solar radii, 0.518 +/- 0.055 solar masses and 4710 +/- 60 K. Conversion uses 695700 km per solar radius and solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. The display axis is sky north, not a measured stellar pole.

sources.position: SIMBAD WD 1856+534 (LP 141-14) basic record, checked 2026-09-23: ICRS position at J2000, reference 2020yCat.1350....0G; Gaia DR3 source 2146576589564898688. https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=WD+1856%2B534

sources.radialVelocity: DERIVED: the white dwarf's featureless spectrum gives no radial velocity. This is the mean of Gaia DR3's values for its co-moving wide companions G 229-20 A (source 2146576757065535360, 17.19 +/- 0.33 km/s) and G 229-20 B (source 2146576761360909056, 17.38 +/- 0.35 km/s), queried from the Gaia archive 2026-09-23. Vanderburg et al. (2020) identify the three stars as one bound triple; the white dwarf's orbital motion around the pair is not included.
